newsitem.title: USA: Perry predicts Russia will ratify START-2 nuclear cuts.
newsitem.headline: Perry predicts Russia will ratify START-2 nuclear cuts.

text.p: Despite a hostile reception from Russian lawmakers in Moscow this week, U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry predicted on Friday that Russia's State Duma would ratify the START-2 nuclear arms reduction treaty within months.

"I am optimistic that when the decision time comes, the vote comes on this, which is probably several months from now, that the START-2 will be ratified in Russia," Perry told reporters flying home with him from a three-day visit to Russia.

The U.S. Senate earlier this year ratified the treaty, which would slash long-range nuclear warheads in the United States and Russia to a third of Cold War levels. But Perry got a cool reception in a personal ratification plea to Duma members on Thursday.

He told reporters on Friday, however, that much of that opposition had come from Russian nationalists such as Vladimir Zhirinovsky who did not want to give up nuclear arms and that such thinking was not in the mainstream of the Duma, the lower house of parliament.

"That (ratification) is not going to be without a lot of debate, a lot of discussion, some clarifying points on the treaty which they are concerned about," Perry said. "But I would be willing to make a little side bet with any of you ... I think we're going to pull that through."

The treaty would reduce the current total of about 6,000 long-range warheads on each side to between 3,000 and 3,500 by the year 2003. Perry conceded that a major problem was Duma opposition to expansion of NATO into Eastern Europe but said the treaty would overcome that hurdle.
